biography.value:
The voice of the Lady of Loss in the sunless temple — the one who has watched Thomas climb from scribe to paladin, and means to finish the work.

Leads with mercy, never power: Shar takes the memory that hurts and calls it kindness, and the priest believes it — every cultist in the building took that deal gratefully. Offers zone of truth and stands in it; answers anything honestly. Combat is the failure state: if it comes, opens with Darkness and repositions — this is their house and it has no windows.

Session 7 kit (CR 6, tuned down from Cultist Hierophant): Nightblade (melee, necrotic), Ray of Loss (ranged, necrotic), Zone of Truth / Darkness / Hold Person / Mass Suggestion via Spellcasting.

A staff of black ash capped with a lens of smoked glass. Held up to a light, the lens does not darken the light — it darkens the eye that looks through it.

Staff, very rare (requires attunement by a Cleric or Wizard)

This staff can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. While holding it, you also gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: Darkness (2 charges), Invisibility (2 charges), Dispel Magic (3 charges), or Counterspell (3 charges).

description.value:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

Harrow Vane makes two Necrotic Burst attacks.

Legendary Action Uses: 2. Immediately after another creature's turn, Harrow Vane can expend a use to take one of the following actions. He regains all expended uses at the start of each of his turns.

Necrotic Burst. Harrow Vane makes one Necrotic Burst attack.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement)

You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws while you wear this cloak.

A quarter of a heart, turned to crystal: dark purple, very nearly black, and the light does not sit on its surface — it crawls under it, slow, like something turning over in deep water. It is the size of two cupped hands, and the chambering and the sheared-off vessels are still there inside the stone like flaws in a gem. It is warm — blood-warm, and stone should be cold — and it beats, slowly, faintly. It does not chip and it does not scratch. It has already been broken.

The vision. The Duskheart requires attunement. The first time you hold it, it shows you one thing. A beautiful green woman, glowing white, leaves crowning her head, weeping. She closes her hands over her own chest, and her heart bursts. The pieces scatter into the dark, hardening as they fly. The burst drives the mists back in a great ring, baring a bare green valley next to a beautiful lake. Where she stood, a tree: grey, leafless, asleep. A single faint heartbeat, and it is over.

While you carry the Duskheart you have advantage on Wisdom saving throws.

Once between dusks, you can lay the shard against a sleeping or willing brow — or the brow of someone who cannot stop you — and take a memory out of them, or put a kinder one in its place. It casts modify memory: the shard is the only component needed, and it asks nothing of you but the choice.

It does not feel like theft. It feels like setting something heavy down.

It is one chamber of a heart — and a heart has four. You cannot shake the feeling that, whole, it could do so much more.
